0.long_answer: XXYY syndrome is a rare variation of Klinefelter syndrome in which affected males have 48 chromosomes (an extra X and an extra Y) instead of the typical 46. This additional chromosomal material leads to a variety of physical, developmental, and neurobehavioral differences when compared to classic Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY). XXYY syndrome is estimated to occur in approximately one in every 50,000 male births, although estimates can range from 1 in 18,000 to 1 in 50,000. This condition was originally considered a variant of Klinefelter syndrome because of the shared features related to testicular dysfunction and hormonal imbalances, but it is now recognized for having its own distinct set of characteristics, including higher rates of developmental delays and learning difficulties.
